result.report:
# KIT-6490: ponyfill inventory

All three ponyfills and the sendBeacon polyfill exist only for **Lightning Locker**, the older Salesforce security mode. Every commit that added them says the bug shows up "when LWS is disabled". Quantic still supports and tests Locker, so I recommend keeping the shims in v4 for the Quantic bundle only, with that bundle pinned to its own ES target. `navigator.sendbeacon` is the one exception: I recommend dropping it.

**Heads-up on the worktree.** I did not edit any repo file. During this research, `git status` showed edits from other sessions:
- `packages/headless/esbuild.mjs` now has `target: ['es2023']`.
- `packages/atomic/rslib.config.mjs`, `packages/atomic/tsconfig.json` and `packages/atomic/tsconfig.lit.json` are modified.

The `esbuild.mjs` change is on the shared `base` config, so the Quantic UMD bundle inherits it too (see recommendations).

Playwright wrote snapshots into `.playwright-mcp/` in the repo. That folder is git-excluded, and I moved its contents to `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alexprudhomme-dev-worktrees-ui-kit-kit-6490-js-target-baseline/92e49a1b-028f-4744-8659-313d3eebe162/scratchpad/research/playwright/`. Other scratch files are in `.../scratchpad/research/{bcd,locker}/`.

## 1. Support table

Browser and Node versions come from MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.10 (`data.json`, timestamp 2026-11-19, from unpkg.com/@mdn/browser-compat-data). "Edge" here means the first EdgeHTML version; Chromium Edge 79 and later has all of these.

| API | Chrome | Edge | Firefox | Safari | iOS Safari | Node | Locker | LWS | Needed in v4? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `globalThis` | 71 | 79 | 65 | 12.1 | 12.2 | 12.0.0 | **No** (L1, L2) | Yes (L5) | Only for Quantic under Locker |
| `Headers` | 42 | 14 | 39 | 10.1 | 10.3 | 18.0.0 | **No** (L2, L3) | Yes (L5) | Only for Quantic under Locker |
| `AbortController` | 66 | 16 | 57 | 12.1 | 12.2 | 14.17.0 | **No** (L2, L4) | Yes (L5) | Only for Quantic under Locker |
| `AbortSignal` | 66 | 16 | 57 | 11.1 | 11.3 | 14.17.0 | **No** (L2) | Yes | Same as above |
| `fetch` | 42 | 14 | 39 | 10.1 | 10.3 | 18.0.0 | Wrapped: first argument is turned into a string (L6) | Yes; blocks `/aura` and `/webruntime` URLs (L7) | Native everywhere |
| `fetch` with signal (`Request.signal`) | 66 | 16 | 57 | 12.1 | 12.2 | 18.0.0 | **No** (no native AbortSignal) | Yes | Only for Quantic under Locker |
| `navigator.sendBeacon` | 39 | 14 | 31 | 11.1 | 11.3 | **Not in Node** (`nodejs: false`) | **No** (L8) | Yes; blocks `/aura` and `/webruntime` URLs (L7) | **No** (see 4) |
| `fetch` with `keepalive` (what Relay uses now) | 66 | 15 | **133** | 13 | 13 | 18.0.0 | Passed straight to native fetch | Yes | Yes (Firefox 133 sets the floor) |
| `Request.duplex` | 131 | 131 | preview | 27.3 | 27.3 | 19.1.0 | n/a | n/a | No (see 5) |

On the Node question: Node has no `sendBeacon`, and the Headless Node CJS build doesn't need it. coveo.analytics only uses beacons for `click` events when `'sendBeacon' in navigator`, and otherwise falls back to fetch (`packages/coveo-analytics/src/client/runtimeEnvironment.ts:47`, `analyticsBeaconClient.ts:38`). With `engines.node` at `^20.9.0`, Node has every other API in the table natively.

**Locker sources:**
- **L1:** the commit message of 66d7ea8e7 (#4701), and `packages/quantic/build-static-resources.js:146-147`, which rewrites `globalThis` to `window` in `coveoua.js` "because `globalThis` is not supported in Locker Service".
- **L2:** a 2018 snapshot of Locker's `SecureWindow` allow-list (github.com/teamchong/SalesforceLWC, `tool/locker-service-viewer_files/locker.js`, last commit 2018-12-14). It has no `AbortController`, `AbortSignal`, `Headers` or `globalThis` entries, while `Request`, `Response` and `fetch` are listed (lines 8110, 8294). This is old evidence, but the 2024–2025 commits confirm the same gaps.
- **L3:** commit e84d61ba4 (#4781): "The headers constructor is not supported in Salesforce where LWS is disabled".
- **L4:** Salesforce, "Evaluate JavaScript Code Compatibility with Lightning Locker" (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lightning-components-security/guide/locker-console-evaluate.html): "AbortController … is not allowed by Lightning Locker". Also commit 4c626064b (#3779).
- **L5:** LWS gives each namespace its own sandbox with the real globals and only "distorts" a few APIs. Its distortion list (github.com/salesforce/lwsec-docs-mirror, `packages/@locker/distortion/docs/distortions.md`, last pushed 2026-06-02) has no entry for globalThis, Headers or AbortController.
- **L6:** in the same 2018 snapshot, `fetch` is wrapped at line 8574, and `sanitizeURLForRequests` (line 1162) does `normalizer.setAttribute('href', url)`. A `Request` object therefore becomes the string `"[object Request]"`, which explains why `fetch(request)` fails under Locker (#4781).
- **L7:** `distortions.md` lines 1397 and 2099: the Window.fetch and Navigator.sendBeacon distortions only reject `/aura` and `/webruntime` URLs.
- **L8:** `SecureNavigator` in the snapshot (lines 7171-7196) exposes only appCodeName, appName, appVersion, cookieEnabled, geolocation, language, onLine, platform, product and userAgent. Also commit 8eb3cddeb (#4074): "sendBeacon … is not supported in Salesforce when LWS is disabled".

## 2. Who uses `dist/quantic/**`, and the history

- **Build:** `packages/headless/build.config.json:13-19` lists the Quantic bundles (search, recommendation, case-assist, insight, commerce). `packages/headless/esbuild.mjs:154-213` builds them as CJS and UMD, injecting the three shims plus `navigator.sendbeacon` (lines 200-205), and inherits `base.target` from line 78.
- **Only consumer:** `@coveo/quantic`.
  - `packages/quantic/package.json:60` (`babel:headless`) runs `@babel/plugin-transform-async-to-generator` (`packages/quantic/babel.config.json`) on `node_modules/@coveo/headless/dist/quantic` and writes to `.tmp/quantic-compiled`.
  - `packages/quantic/build-static-resources.js:57-86` copies the result into `force-app/main/default/staticresources/coveoheadless/**`. That folder is gitignored (`packages/quantic/.gitignore:39`) and published through Quantic's `files` (`package.json:18`).
  - `packages/quantic/turbo.json:5,9,22` wires it into the build.
  - `scripts/npm/setup-quantic.js` only copies `force-app/main/default` into a customer's SFDX project, so it doesn't read Headless directly.
  - `git grep dist/quantic` finds no other package.
- **Shipped to all npm users:** `dist/quantic` is inside `files: ["dist/"]` (`packages/headless/package.json:12-14`), so every Headless npm install gets it. There is no `exports` entry for it.
- **Possible external consumer:** the Coveo for Salesforce (SFINT) package. Commit 66d7ea8e7 says "SFINT package tests are running on Locker". I can't verify this from the repo.
- **Why the async transform exists:** commit ce8d7c8fa (#4620, SFINT-5784): "Salesforce LWS has a problem with static resources files using async/await on Firefox".

## 3. Locker vs LWS in 2026

- **New orgs default to LWS:** "New orgs have Lightning Web Security for Lightning web components and Aura components enabled by default. If you create an org from a template, then that org inherits the LWS setting of the template." (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lightning-components-security/guide/lws-enable.html)
- **Locker is still common and sometimes required:**
  - "Lightning Locker is enabled by default for all new Aura sites in Experience Cloud." LWS only "aims to replace Lightning Locker". "For the B2B store and the D2C store LWR templates in Commerce Cloud, LWS isn't enabled by default and can't be enabled." (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/communities-dev/guide/communities-dev-security-locker-csp.html)
  - Lightning Out and Lightning Components for Visualforce require Locker: "To use Lightning Out, you must use Lightning Locker… Lightning Out isn't supported when LWS is enabled." (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lightning-components-security/guide/get-started-compare-lws-locker.html)
  - Admins can still turn LWS off in Session Settings.
  - I found no announced retirement date for Locker. The Locker API Viewer page (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/component-library/tools/locker-service-viewer) now redirects to an empty page.
- **Quantic supports both modes:**
  - `packages/quantic/README.md:53-55` describes two scratch orgs, "LWS enabled" and "LWS disabled, Locker Service enabled".
  - `packages/quantic/playwright.config.ts:51,58` defines `LWS-enabled` and `LWS-disabled` e2e projects.
  - The scratch org definitions use `lockerServiceNext` true or false (`packages/quantic/config/lws-{enabled,disabled}-scratch-def.json:18`).
  - Coveo's public Quantic page (https://www.coveo.com/en/solutions/ai-customer-service/quantic) still says "Is Coveo Quantic compatible with Lightning Web Security? No. Quantic components rely on JavaScript await/async functions which are not currently supported by Lightning Web Security." That contradicts the repo, which tests on LWS and transforms async code for it. It's a docs fix to raise, not a technical constraint.

## 4. Headless, Relay and coveo.analytics source

All greps ran on `packages/headless/src/**/*.ts`, excluding tests.

- **No imports** of `abortcontroller-polyfill`, `headers-polyfill` or `navigator.sendbeacon`. The packages are only used by `ponyfills/*.js` and `esbuild.mjs:204`.
- They are still listed as runtime `dependencies` (`packages/headless/package.json:107,112,113`), even though only the Quantic bundle uses them and it inlines them. Every npm consumer installs them for nothing.
- **`globalThis`:** zero direct uses. The CDN bundle has 31 matches, all from bundled dependencies: dayjs UMD wrappers guarded with `typeof globalThis`, `globalThis.Iterator` (from an immer-style dependency), `globalThis.fetch`, TextEncoder checks, and the UMD wrapper itself.
- **`AbortController`, used natively:**
  - `src/api/search/api-calls-queue.ts:14`
  - `src/api/generated-answer/generated-answer-client.ts:93`
  - `src/utils/fetch-event-source/fetch.ts:113`. This one is written `AbortController ? new AbortController() : null`; the guard is useless because a missing global throws a ReferenceError. That's a small v4 cleanup.
- **`fetch`:** called as `fetch(url, requestData)` in `src/api/platform-client.ts:59`, with an optional `signal` (line 35). RTK Query's `fetchBaseQuery` is used in `src/api/knowledge/answer-slice.ts:39-41`.
- **`new Headers`:** only in SSR code: `src/ssr/common/augment-preprocess-request.ts:36` and `src/ssr-next/common/augment-preprocess-request.ts:36`. RTK Query also uses it internally.
- **`sendBeacon`:** no uses in Headless.
- **Relay no longer uses `sendBeacon`.** It sends with `fetch(url, {keepalive: true, …})` (`packages/relay/src/environment/browser/browser.ts:28-31`). The 2.0.0 breaking change says: "Relay now uses fetch with keepalive instead of navigator.sendBeacon … (including Firefox 133+)" (`packages/relay/CHANGELOG.md:39-45`).
  - So the reason for #4074 is gone. The only `sendBeacon` user left is coveo.analytics, which falls back to fetch when beacons aren't available.
  - Under Locker, `keepalive` goes straight to the native fetch (L6).
- **Side note:** `packages/create-atomic/src/client.ts:2` imports `abortcontroller-polyfill`, which is dead code on Node ≥20.9 (`packages/create-atomic/package.json:68`).

## 5. The code-replacer plugin (`esbuild.mjs:136-152`, `160-190`, `208`)

**What it does:** in the Quantic bundles only, it uses a regex to rewrite `answer-slice.ts`'s `})(updatedArgs, api, extraOptions);`. It adds:
- a `fetchFn` that copies the `Request`'s fields into a plain options object (`options.body = await request.text()`, `duplex: 'half'`) and calls `fetch(url, options)`;
- `{...api, signal: null}`.

**Why each part exists:**
1. **`fetchFn` / `fetch(url, options)`:** Locker's wrapped fetch turns its first argument into a string, so `fetch(request)` breaks (#4781, L6).
2. **`signal: null`:** RTK's `new Request(..., {signal})` gets the *ponyfill* AbortSignal from the injected `AbortController`. The native `Request` rejects it: "Failed to convert value to 'AbortSignal'" (#4731).
3. **`duplex: 'half'`:** not needed. Chrome only requires `duplex` for `ReadableStream` bodies, and here the body is already a string. It does no harm (BCD `api.Request.duplex`).

**Dependencies:**
- It does not depend on the ES target: it's a source-text replacement on the `.ts` file before transpiling.
- It does depend on the ponyfills: (2) exists only because of the AbortSignal ponyfill, and (1) only because of Locker. Under LWS or in plain browsers, neither is needed.
- **It is fragile:** `String.replace` silently does nothing if a formatter or refactor changes that line. Right now it still matches: all five `dist/quantic/**/headless.js` files contain the replacement (one "must be a Request object" match, two "duplex" matches each). It needs a build-time check that fails when nothing matches.

## Recommendations

| Item | Recommendation | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `global-this-shim.js` | **Keep, Quantic bundle only.** The CDN and npm builds don't use it, and none of the v4 browser or Node floors need it. | If dropped, Quantic stops loading in Locker orgs (#4701). Moving it into the Quantic package would need Quantic's own bundling step, which it doesn't have today: it only runs babel. |
| `headers-shim.js` + `headers-polyfill` 5.0.1 | **Keep, Quantic bundle only.** Move the package from `dependencies` to `devDependencies`, since it's inlined. | If dropped, RTK Query (generated-answer feedback) breaks under Locker (#4781). Moving it to devDependencies is low risk; check the CDN and npm bundles don't reference it (they don't today). |
| `abortable-fetch-shim.js` + `abortcontroller-polyfill` | **Keep, Quantic bundle only.** Move to `devDependencies` in Headless; drop it from create-atomic (Node ≥20.9). | If dropped, every `api-calls-queue` and generated-answer call breaks under Locker (#3779). Keep the `signal: null` replacement paired with this shim. |
| `navigator.sendbeacon` 0.0.20 | **Drop.** Relay ≥2.0 uses fetch with keepalive, and coveo.analytics already falls back to fetch. | Low. Under Locker, legacy UA click events go through fetch instead of a beacon, so they're less reliable on page unload. Do a quick Locker e2e smoke test of UA clicks. |
| `codeReplacerPlugin` | **Keep while Locker is supported, and make it fail the build when it matches nothing.** Remove `duplex`. Better: replace the regex with a real `fetchFn` option chosen by a build-time `define`, such as `process.env.QUANTIC_BUNDLE`. | If it silently stops matching, generated-answer feedback breaks in Locker orgs. |
| Quantic bundle ES target | **Give `quanticUmd` its own target**, pinned to `es2020` or whatever Locker and LWS were tested with, instead of inheriting `base.target`. | Today `quanticUmd` spreads `base`, so another session's in-progress change of `base.target` to `es2023` would also change the Salesforce bundle. Locker's evaluator and LWS on Firefox have already broken on newer syntax (async/await, #4620). Raising the Quantic syntax level needs a separate Locker and LWS e2e run. |
| Overall | Make **"Quantic bundle = Salesforce compatibility layer"** an explicit decision in the ADR. The public CDN and npm baselines need no ponyfills. Revisit removing them when Quantic drops Locker support; that is a product decision, since Salesforce still defaults Aura Experience Cloud sites to Locker and Lightning Out requires it. | — |

corrections.claim: Heads-up: packages/headless/esbuild.mjs now has `target: ['es2023']` (on the shared `base` config).
corrections.problem: The file says something else now. Another session is still changing it, so the value moves.
corrections.correction: Right now `git diff packages/headless/esbuild.mjs` shows `-  target: ['es2020'],` / `+  target: ['es2022'],` at line 78. The point still holds: `quanticUmd` goes through `buildBrowserConfig`, which spreads `...base` first (esbuild.mjs:257-265), so the Quantic bundle inherits whatever value `base.target` has. The ADR should quote the target it decides on, not a snapshot of someone else's work in progress.

corrections.claim: Drop navigator.sendbeacon: low risk, because coveo.analytics already falls back to fetch. Under Locker, legacy UA click events would go through fetch instead of a beacon, so they are less reliable on page unload.
corrections.problem: This has two problems. (1) The fallback covers only the click path. `BrowserRuntime` adds a `beforeunload` listener that calls `this.beaconClient.sendEvent(...)` for every buffered request with no `isAvailable()` check. `sendEvent` throws when `'sendBeacon' in navigator` is false, so in Locker those buffered events are dropped with an unhandled rejection instead of going through fetch. (2) The comparison is wrong. In Locker today there is no real beacon: the `navigator.sendbeacon` 0.0.20 package is a global polyfill that assigns `navigator.sendBeacon` to an XMLHttpRequest sender. That sender is async, and becomes synchronous only when `window.event` is unload or beforeunload. So dropping it swaps XHR for fetch on clicks and loses the beforeunload flush. It does not swap a beacon for fetch.
corrections.correction: Dropping sendBeacon is still reasonable, but the risk statement needs both points: the beforeunload flush in coveo.analytics throws and loses events when sendBeacon is missing, and today's Locker behavior is an XHR shim, not a beacon. Before dropping the polyfill, add an `isAvailable()` guard with a fetch fallback (keepalive) to the beforeunload path in coveo.analytics, or accept the loss. The Locker smoke test should cover page unload with buffered events, not only clicks.

corrections.claim: Code-replacer section: `signal: null` exists only because of the AbortSignal ponyfill, and '(1) only because of Locker. Under LWS or in plain browsers, neither is needed.'
corrections.problem: This reads as if the shims only take effect under Locker. They don't. esbuild `inject` replaces every free reference to `AbortController`, `AbortSignal`, `fetch`, `Headers` and `globalThis` in the Quantic bundle with the ponyfill exports at build time, whatever the runtime. `abortable-fetch-shim.js` calls `abortableFetchFactory({fetch})` without passing a native `AbortController`. `polyfillNeeded()` therefore always returns true, and the exported `AbortController` is always the polyfill class. The same bundle ships to LWS orgs, so LWS orgs also run the ponyfill AbortSignal and also need `signal: null`. PR #4781's description says #4731 fixed 'a similar issue in Salesforce environment where the security setting Lightning Web Security (LWS) was enabled'.
corrections.correction: For as long as the shims are injected, `signal: null` is needed in both LWS and Locker orgs. Only the `fetchFn` (`fetch(url, options)`) part is Locker-specific. The table's 'Only for Quantic under Locker' should read 'only in the Quantic bundle (which then uses them in LWS and Locker orgs alike)'. Otherwise the ADR could suggest an LWS-only bundle that drops `signal: null` while keeping the shims.

corrections.claim: Lightning Out and Lightning Components for Visualforce require Locker ('Lightning Out isn't supported when LWS is enabled').
corrections.problem: That sentence applies to Lightning Out (Beta) only. Lightning Out 2.0, GA in Winter '26, replaces the beta and runs embedded LWCs under LWS. Its comparison page says 'Lightning Locker isn't supported'.
corrections.correction: Make it 'Lightning Out (Beta) and Lightning Components for Visualforce (Beta) require Locker; Lightning Out 2.0 (GA Winter '26) uses LWS.' That weakens the case that Locker is still required, though Aura Experience Cloud sites still default to Locker.

corrections.claim: Locker is still common and sometimes required: 'For the B2B store and the D2C store LWR templates in Commerce Cloud, LWS isn't enabled by default and can't be enabled.'
corrections.problem: The sentence is used as evidence for Locker, but LWR sites don't run Lightning Locker at all. A B2B or D2C LWR store without LWS runs with no sandbox, not with Locker, so native AbortController, Headers and globalThis are available there.
corrections.correction: Cite this as evidence that some Salesforce surfaces run without LWS, not that they need Locker. The Locker-specific evidence is the Aura-sites default ('Lightning Locker is enabled by default for all new Aura sites'), Lightning Out (Beta), and orgs that turn LWS off.

corrections.claim: Support table row `Request.duplex`: Chrome 131, Edge 131, Safari 27.3, iOS 27.3, Node 19.1.0, used to argue that `duplex: 'half'` is harmless.

# KIT-6490: Node floor and build-tooling impact

Scratch evidence is in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alexprudhomme-dev-worktrees-ui-kit-kit-6490-js-target-baseline/92e49a1b-028f-4744-8659-313d3eebe162/scratchpad/research/`: `features.mjs` and `features.out` (feature probe on real Node binaries), `esparse.cjs` (acorn parse of built outputs), `published/` (npm install of `@coveo/headless@3.59.0`) and `tm/` (minimal repro). I modified no repo files.

## Headline findings
- **The published Headless CommonJS entry is broken today on every Node version.** `require('@coveo/headless')` on 3.59.0 throws `TypeError: import_bueno3.StringValue is not a constructor` on Node 20.20.2, 22.23.4 and 24.22.1. I reproduced this in `published/`.
  - **Root cause:** in `packages/bueno/package.json`, line 14 sets `"type": "module"` and line 22 points the `require` condition at `./dist/bueno.js`. That file is esbuild CommonJS output (`module.exports = …`, `packages/bueno/dist/bueno.js:60`). Node loads it as ESM because of the `"type"` field, and `require` gets back an empty namespace.
  - **Confirmation:** when I pointed bueno's `require` at `./dist/bueno.esm.js` in the scratch install, `require('@coveo/headless')` and `buildSearchEngine` worked on 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22.
  - **Since when:** bueno got `"type": "module"` on 2025-02-26 (commit ab8931e39, #4987), and Headless's node CJS has required `@coveo/bueno` externally since 2025-05-28 (bc4699659, #4921).
  - **Jest 29 (default CJS mode) also fails,** for a different reason: `@coveo/relay` → `uuid/dist-node/index.js` gives `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'`.
  - **What it means:** nobody can be using `dist/cjs` in plain Node today, so dropping CJS in v4 costs very little. It also means the v3 CJS bug is worth a separate bug fix. I filed nothing.
- **Headless's npm ESM already ships ES2022 syntax.** `dist/esm` fails an ES2021 parse in 18 files (class fields, e.g. `dist/esm/api/analytics/base-analytics.js:11`) and parses at ES2022. Only the esbuild outputs (`cdn/`, `dist/cjs`, `dist/quantic`) are held to `es2020` (`packages/headless/esbuild.mjs:78`).
- **Atomic's CDN build already ships ES2022 syntax and has an implicit browser baseline.** 120 of 436 `cdn/*.js` files contain `#private` and fail an ES2021 parse; all pass at ES2022.
  - `rsbuild.cdn.mjs` sets no browserslist, so Rsbuild 2.1.13's default applies: `chrome >= 107, edge >= 107, firefox >= 104, safari >= 16`, "baseline widely available on 2025-05-01" (`node_modules/.pnpm/@rsbuild+core@2.1.13_core-js@3.51.0/node_modules/@rsbuild/core/dist/626.js:1101-1105`, `dist/constants.d.ts:31-33`).
  - Atomic's `dist/esm` with rslib `syntax: 'es2021'` maps to chrome 91 / firefox 80 / safari 16.3 (rslib 0.23.2 `ESX_TO_BROWSERSLIST`). For `es2022` it maps to chrome 94 / edge 94 / firefox 93 / safari 16.4, and `es2023` is the same as `es2022`.

## 2. Node release dates

## 3. What dropping Node 20 unlocks (and what needs ≥22.12)
I probed the real binaries v20.20.2 (V8 11.3), v22.23.4 (V8 12.4) and v24.22.1 (V8 13.6); results are in `features.out`.

**`require(esm)`** (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/modules.html, history table):
- Added in 22.0.0 and 20.17.0, behind a flag.
- Unflagged in **22.12.0** and 20.19.0.
- The experimental warning was removed in 22.13.0 and 20.19.0.
- It is "no longer experimental" in **24.15.0** and 25.4.0.
- In the 22.x docs it is still "Stability 1.2 – Release candidate".
- If the required graph has top-level await, it throws `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`.

**`fetch`, `Headers`, `Request`, `Response`:** unflagged in 18.0.0, stable in 21.0.0. **`AbortController`:** stable since 15.4.0. **`AbortSignal.timeout`:** 17.3.0. **`AbortSignal.any`:** 20.3.0 and 18.17.0. Source: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/globals.html. All are present on 20, 22 and 24, so the Headers and abortable-fetch ponyfills are never needed on any Node line in `engines`.

**`navigator` global:** 21.0.0, still "1.1 Active development". It is absent on 20 and present on 22 and 24. **`navigator.sendBeacon` is absent on every Node version**, so Headless must keep feature-detecting it on the server.

**ES built-ins:**
| Feature | Node 20 | Node 22 | Node 24 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ES2022 (class fields, `#private`, static blocks, `at`, `Object.hasOwn`, error `cause`) | yes | yes | yes |
| ES2023 (`toSorted`, `with`, `findLast`) | yes | yes | yes |
| ES2024: `Object.groupBy`, `Map.groupBy`, `Promise.withResolvers`, resizable ArrayBuffer and `transfer` | **no** | yes | yes |
| ES2024: RegExp `v` flag, `isWellFormed`, `Atomics.waitAsync` | yes | yes | yes |
| ES2025: Set methods, Iterator helpers | no | **yes** | yes |
| ES2025: `Promise.try`, `RegExp.escape`, `Float16Array` | no | no | yes |
| `Array.fromAsync` | no | yes | yes |
| `Error.isError`, `using` | no | no | yes |
| Import attributes `with { type: 'json' }` | yes | yes | yes |

So **Node 22 is the first line with full ES2024 built-ins.** Dropping Node 20 lets Headless's node output use `lib` ES2024 without polyfills, and target `node22`.

**The `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` comment** (`packages/headless/esbuild.mjs:224-233`, `resolveSubpath`) refers to Node 20.9–20.18 and 22.11.x. Both are admitted by today's `^20.9.0 || ^22.11.0` and have no unflagged `require(esm)`. With a floor of `^22.12.0`:
- `require()` of an `.mjs` works without a flag, so the alias workaround for coveo.analytics deep imports becomes unnecessary for the node build.
- More importantly, **Headless can ship ESM only.** I verified that `require()` of the published `dist/esm/index.js`, `commerce.index.js` and `ssr-next.index.js` succeeds on 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22 (125, 65 and 112 exports), so there is no top-level await in those graphs. Node 18 throws `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`.
- To go ESM only: drop `dist/cjs` and the `require` conditions, and keep a `default` condition pointing at ESM. `require('@coveo/headless')` then resolves through `default` to `require(esm)` on ≥22.12.

Jest users then need `transformIgnorePatterns` or ESM mode. But the current CJS entry already fails in Jest (the uuid issue above), so this is not a regression.
- **Caveat 2:** only the 24.15+ and 25.4+ lines call `require(esm)` stable. On 22.x it is "release candidate".

**Context in the repo:**
- KIT-6672 (from PLAN.md): the future `@coveo/headless-ssr` is ESM only. I found no in-repo doc for it.
- `@coveo/headless-react` is **already ESM only**: its `exports` (`package.json:22`) have no `require` condition, and it is built with tsc ES2022.
- Thermidor already decided "no CommonJS to npm, ES2022" (`packages/thermidor/docs/internal/adr/ADR-005-build-process.md:16`). Lines 80 and 97 of that ADR note its `^22.11.0` floor needs `--experimental-require-module` on 22.11.x, an argument for `^22.12.0` everywhere.

## 4. esbuild target for the node output
- esbuild accepts `nodeX[.Y.Z]` targets, transforms **syntax only** and adds **no polyfills** (https://esbuild.github.io/api/#target).

- So `node22` ≈ ES2023/ES2024 syntax with nothing lowered (ES2023 and ES2024 added almost no lowerable syntax).

## Recommendation for v4 `engines.node` (input to KIT-6387)
- **Use `^22.12.0 || ^24.11.0 || ^26.0.0` for every public package**, wrappers included.
  - 22.12.0 is the first 22.x with unflagged `require(esm)`, which ESM-only Headless and headless-react need for CJS consumers. It matches create-ui and Angular 20/21's floor.
  - 26 has been Active LTS since 2026-10-28.
  - Alternative: `^22.13.0` avoids the ExperimentalWarning that 22.12 prints.
- Ship Headless ESM only on npm, consistent with headless-react, thermidor and the headless-ssr decision. Drop `dist/cjs` (or, if CJS is kept, fix bueno's `require` condition and set the esbuild node target to `node22.12`).
- Keep the Quantic UMD on its own target and ponyfill decision.
- **Open questions for Alex:**
  1. Node 22 reaches EOL on 2027-04-30, inside v4's life. Should v4 drop it in a minor, or start at `^24.11.0 || ^26.0.0`? Angular 22 already requires `^22.22.3`.
  2. Is the v3 CJS breakage (bueno `require` → CJS `.js` in a `"type": "module"` package) worth a separate bug fix?
